ws.practice.hint: Log question sets, see weak topics first, learn from every mistake.
ws.practice.setsLede: Did some questions? Jot down how it went. Your weakest topics float to the top.
ws.practice.needTopic: Pick or type a topic first.
ws.practice.setsEmpty: No sets yet. Try a handful of questions, then log them here.
ws.practice.weakFirstSub: Lowest accuracy at the top. Start there.
ws.practice.errorsLede: Every wrong answer is a clue. Note why it happened and what you’ll do next time.
ws.practice.question: The question
ws.practice.lesson: Lesson / what I’ll do next time
ws.practice.lessonPh: e.g. Underline what the question actually asks.
ws.practice.needQuestion: Write down the question (a few words is fine).
ws.practice.errorsEmpty: No mistakes logged. That’s either great news or a sign to try more questions 😉
ws.practice.insight.unknown: Mostly gaps in knowledge: turn these into cards and review them.
ws.practice.insight.misread: Mostly misreading: slow down and underline what is asked.
ws.practice.insight.careless: Mostly careless slips: build in a quick check before moving on.
ws.practice.insight.time: Mostly running out of time: practise a few sets under the clock.
ws.practice.insight.reasoning: Mostly reasoning slips: rework these step by step, out loud.
ws.practice.noLesson: No lesson yet. What would you do differently?
ws.why.hint: Ask “why?” about a fact, again and again, until you hit bedrock.
ws.why.lede: Pick one fact from your notes. You’ll explain why it’s true, then why that is, up to five levels deep.
ws.why.factPh: e.g. Arteries have thicker walls than veins.
ws.why.lookupsSub: The whys you couldn’t answer yet. Gaps found now are gaps the exam can’t find.
ws.why.foundPh: The answer, in your own words
ws.why.empty: No chains yet. Start with any fact that you just accept.
ws.why.answerPh: Answer from what you already know, in a sentence or two.
ws.why.alt: Stuck? Try “why here and not elsewhere?” or “what if it were different?”
ws.why.gapMark: Couldn’t answer: it’s on your look-up list.
ws.why.doneText: Nicely tied down. Every answer is one more route back to this fact.
ws.why.doneGap: You found a gap. Look it up and the chain gets stronger.
ws.examples.hint: Pin an abstract idea to varied, concrete examples.
ws.examples.lede: One example can mislead. Collect a few that look different but share the same core, plus one that doesn’t fit.
ws.examples.empty: No ideas yet. What’s something abstract you’re learning?
ws.examples.ph.course: A case from your lectures or book…
ws.examples.ph.non: Something that looks similar but isn’t it…
ws.examples.needMore: Aim for at least two, of different kinds.
ws.examples.enough: ✨ Nice variety. Now, what do they share?
ws.examples.common: What do they have in common?
ws.examples.commonHint: That shared part is the idea itself.
ws.examples.storyPh: A person, a patient, a client, a bug… who wants what, and what happens?
ws.examples.storyHint: Each part of a story cues the next.
ws.notes.hint: Cornell, question notes, concept maps, tables, one-pagers and objective checklists.
ws.notes.about.cornell: Notes on the right, cue questions on the left, a summary at the bottom. Later, cover the notes and answer the cues.
ws.notes.about.questions: Every heading is a question. Your notes turn into a quiz you wrote yourself.
ws.notes.about.map: Ideas and labelled links between them. The labels are where the learning happens.
ws.notes.about.table: Easily confused things side by side, on the features that tell them apart.
ws.notes.about.summary: A whole topic on one page, written from memory first.
ws.notes.about.objectives: Paste your course’s learning objectives and tick each one only when you can answer it with the book closed.
ws.notes.titlePh.questions: e.g. Why did the Weimar Republic collapse?
ws.notes.title: Title
ws.notes.empty: Nothing here yet. Your first note is one tap away.
ws.notes.cornellHint: Write notes on the right; add a cue question on the left within a day.
ws.notes.qHint: Turn each heading into a how, why or what-if question.
ws.notes.summaryPh: The whole page in two or three sentences.
ws.notes.mapHint: Add 8–15 key ideas, then connect them with labelled links. Redraw it from memory in a few days.
ws.notes.relPh: causes, requires, is an example of…
ws.notes.tableHint: Columns are the confusable things; rows are the features that tell them apart.
ws.notes.summaryHint: Close the book first. Write the 3–5 main ideas and how they connect. Then check and add what you missed below.
ws.notes.memoryPh: The big ideas, and how they fit together…
ws.notes.missedPh: These are the bits to review next.
ws.notes.objHint: Copy the objectives from your syllabus or lecture slides, one per line.
ws.notes.pastePh:
Explain how the kidney concentrates urine
Compare type 1 and type 2 diabetes
…
ws.notes.objTick: Read each one as a question. Tick it only if you can answer with the book closed.
ws.memory.hint: Mnemonics, a memory palace and chunking for lists that won’t stick.
ws.memory.acronymLede: For lists without their own logic. List the items, look at the first letters, then make a silly, vivid sentence.
ws.memory.sentenceHint: Sillier and more personal is better.
ws.memory.palaceLede: Pick a place you know by heart, walk a fixed route through it and leave one vivid image at each stop.
ws.memory.palaceEmpty: No palaces yet. Your home is a great first one.
ws.memory.imagePh: e.g. A glowing battery melting into the door handle
ws.memory.imageHint: Exaggerated, moving, a bit absurd, and touching the spot.
ws.memory.chunkLede: Paste a long list or number. It splits into small groups; give each group a meaningful label.
ws.memory.chunkEmpty: Your groups will show up here.
